61.translation: Thus, by two verses, dependence on prakṛti, dependence on nature, and dependence on action have been stated according to the Sāṅkhya and other views. Now he states his own view in the two verses beginning ‘the Lord.’ The Lord, the inner ruler, dwells in the middle of the heart of all beings. Doing what? Causing all beings to revolve by māyā, His own power, setting them in motion in their respective actions, just as in the world a stage-director causes artificial beings mounted on a wooden machine to revolve. Or the machines are bodies; the beings mounted on them are the living selves who identify with the body; He causes them to revolve. This is the meaning. Thus also the mantra of the Śvetāśvataras: ‘One God, hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings, overseer of action, dwelling in all beings, witness, consciousness, alone, without guṇas.’ And the Antaryāmin Brāhmaṇa: ‘He who, standing within the self, controls the self from within, whom the self does not know, whose body is the self—He is your Self, the inner ruler, immortal,’ and so forth.
word_for_word: tad evaṃ śloka-dvayena sāṃkhya-ādi-matena prakṛti-pāratantryaṃ svabhāva-pāratantryaṃ karma-pāratantryaṃ ca uktam

idānīṃ sva-matam āha — īśvara iti dvābhyām
now he states his own view in the two verses beginning ‘the Lord’
sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛdaya-madhye īśvaraḥ antaryāmī tiṣṭhati
the Lord, the inner ruler, dwells in the middle of the heart of all beings
kiṃ kurvan
doing what?
sarvāṇi bhūtāni māyayā nija-śaktyā bhrāmayan
causing all beings to revolve by māyā, His own power
tat-tat-karmasu pravartayan
setting them in motion in their respective actions
yathā dāru-yantram ārūḍhāni kṛtrimāṇi bhūtāni sūtradhāraḥ loke bhrāmayati tadvat
just as in the world a stage-director causes artificial beings mounted on a wooden machine to revolve
yad vā yantrāṇi śarīrāṇi

ārūḍhāni bhūtāni deha-abhimāninaḥ jīvān

bhrāmayan iti arthaḥ

tathā ca śvetāśvatarāṇāṃ mantraḥ
thus also the mantra of the Śvetāśvataras
eko devaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarva-vyāpī sarva-bhūta-antarātmā
‘one God, hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings’
karmādhyakṣaḥ sarva-bhūta-adhivāsaḥ sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaḥ ca iti
‘overseer of action, dwelling in all beings, witness, consciousness, alone, without guṇas’

ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmānam antaraḥ yamayati

eṣa te ātmā antaryāmī amṛtaḥ ity-ādi
‘He is your Self, the inner ruler, immortal,’ and so forth

62.translation: With ‘Him.’ Since in this way all living selves are dependent on the Supreme Lord, therefore, abandoning ego, with every disposition, with the whole self, go for refuge to that Lord alone. Then, by His grace alone, you will attain supreme quietude and the supreme Lord’s abode, everlasting, eternal.
word_for_word: tam iti
with ‘Him’
yasmāt evaṃ sarve jīvāḥ parameśvara-paratantrāḥ
since in this way all living selves are dependent on the Supreme Lord
tasmāt ahaṅkāraṃ parityajya
therefore, abandoning ego
sarva-bhāvena sarvātmanā tam īśvaram eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha
with every disposition, with the whole self, go for refuge to that Lord alone
tataḥ tasya eva prasādāt parām upaśāntiṃ
then, by His grace alone, supreme quietude
sthānaṃ ca pārameśvaraṃ śāśvataṃ nityaṃ prāpsyasi
and the supreme Lord’s abode, everlasting, eternal, you will attain

63.translation: Concluding the meaning of the entire Gītā, he says ‘thus.’ Thus, in this manner, knowledge has been declared, taught, to you by Me, the omniscient and supremely compassionate. Of what kind? More secret even than secret knowledge such as secret mantra and yoga. Having reflected on, examined, this entire Gītā teaching taught by Me, afterward act just as you wish. When this has been reflected upon, your delusion will cease. This is the intention.
word_for_word: sarva-gītārtham upasaṃharan āha — iti iti
concluding the meaning of the entire Gītā, he says ‘thus’
iti anena prakāreṇa tubhyaṃ sarvajñena parama-kāruṇikena mayā jñānam ākhyātam upadiṣṭam
thus, in this manner, knowledge has been declared, taught, to you by Me, the omniscient and supremely compassionate
kathaṃ-bhūtam
of what kind?
guhyāt gopyāt rahasya-mantra-yoga-ādi-jñānāt api guhyataram
more secret even than secret knowledge such as secret mantra and yoga
etat mayā upadiṣṭaṃ gītā-śāstram aśeṣataḥ vimṛśya paryālocya
having reflected on, examined, this entire Gītā teaching taught by Me
paścāt yathā icchasi tathā kuru
afterward act just as you wish
etasmin paryālocite sati tava moho nivartiṣyate iti bhāvaḥ
when this has been reflected upon, your delusion will cease: this is the intention

64.translation: For one unable to examine the exceedingly profound Gītā teaching without remainder, out of compassion He Himself gathers its essence and states it, in the three verses beginning ‘the most secret of all.’ Hear My word, most secret among all secrets, although stated here and there, and now to be said again, repeatedly. He states the reason for speaking repeatedly: considering that you are exceedingly, firmly dear to Me, for that very reason I will state what is beneficial to you. Or: having ascertained that you are dear to Me and that what is to be stated by Me is firm, furnished with all means of knowledge, therefore I will state it to you. This is the meaning. Some read ‘dṛḍhamati,’ ‘of firm understanding.’
word_for_word: ati-gambhīraṃ gītā-śāstram aśeṣataḥ paryālocayitum aśaknuvataḥ
for one unable to examine the exceedingly profound Gītā teaching without remainder
kṛpayā svayam eva tasya sāraṃ saṃgṛhya kathayati
out of compassion He Himself gathers its essence and states it
sarva-guhyatamam iti tribhiḥ
in the three verses beginning ‘the most secret of all’
sarvebhyaḥ api guhyebhyaḥ guhyatamaṃ me vacaḥ
My word, most secret among all secrets
tatra tatra uktam api bhūyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ api vakṣyamāṇaṃ śṛṇu
although stated here and there, hear it again, repeatedly, as it is now to be said
punaḥ punaḥ kathane hetum āha
he states the reason for speaking repeatedly
dṛḍham atyantaṃ me mama tvam iṣṭaḥ priyaḥ asi iti matvā
considering that you are exceedingly, firmly dear to Me
tata eva hetoḥ te hitaṃ vakṣyāmi
for that very reason I will state what is beneficial to you
yad vā tvam mama iṣṭaḥ asi
or: you are dear to Me
mayā vakṣyamāṇaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ sarva-pramāṇa-upetam iti niścitya
and having ascertained that what is to be stated by Me is firm, furnished with all means of knowledge
tataḥ te vakṣyāmi iti arthaḥ
therefore I will state it to you: this is the meaning
dṛḍhamatiḥ iti kecit paṭhanti
some read ‘dṛḍhamati,’ ‘of firm understanding’

65.translation: He states that with ‘mind in Me.’ Become one whose mind is in Me; become one whose thought is in Me; become My devotee alone; become one who sacrifices to Me, one whose habit is worship of Me; bow to Me alone. Continuing thus, through knowledge obtained by My grace, you will come to Me alone, will attain Me. Do not make doubt here. For you are dear to Me; therefore I truly promise you, make a promise to you, exactly as it will be.
word_for_word: tad eva āha — man-manā iti
he states that with ‘mind in Me’
man-manā bhava
become one whose mind is in Me
mat-cittaḥ bhava
become one whose thought is in Me
mama eva bhaktaḥ bhava
become My devotee alone
mad-yājī mad-yajana-śīlo bhava
become one who sacrifices to Me, one whose habit is worship of Me
mām eva namaskuru
bow to Me alone
evaṃ vartamānaḥ tvam mat-prasādāt labdha-jñānena mām eva eṣyasi prāpsyasi
continuing thus, through knowledge obtained by My grace, you will come to Me alone, will attain Me
atra ca saṃśayaṃ mā kārṣīḥ
do not make doubt here
tvaṃ hi me priyaḥ asi
for you are dear to Me
ataḥ satyaṃ yathā bhavati evaṃ tubhyam ahaṃ pratijāne pratijñāṃ karomi
therefore I truly promise you, make a promise to you, exactly as it will be

66.translation: Then he states what is even more secret with ‘all.’ With firm faith that through devotion to Me alone everything will be accomplished, abandoning servitude to injunction, become one who takes refuge in Me alone. Continuing thus, do not grieve, do not make sorrow, thinking that sin may arise because of abandonment of action. For I will free you, who take refuge in Me alone, from all sins.
word_for_word: tataḥ api guhyatamam āha — sarva iti
then he states what is even more secret with ‘all’
mad-bhaktyā eva sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati iti dṛḍha-viśvāsena
with firm faith that through devotion to Me alone everything will be accomplished
vidhi-kaikaryaṃ tyaktvā
abandoning servitude to injunction
mad-eka-śaraṇaḥ bhava
become one who takes refuge in Me alone
evaṃ vartamānaḥ karma-tyāga-nimittaṃ pāpaṃ syāt iti mā śucaḥ śokaṃ mā kārṣīḥ
continuing thus, do not grieve, do not make sorrow, thinking that sin may arise because of abandonment of action
yataḥ tvā tvāṃ mad-eka-śaraṇaṃ sarva-pāpebhyaḥ ahaṃ mokṣayiṣyāmi
for I will free you, who take refuge in Me alone, from all sins

67.translation: Having thus taught the truth of the meaning of the Gītā, he states a rule for setting its tradition in motion with ‘this.’ This truth of the meaning of the Gītā is not to be spoken by you to one without austerity, one lacking performance of his own dharma; nor is it ever to be spoken to one without devotion, one devoid of devotion to the teacher and to the Lord; nor is it to be spoken to one unwilling to serve, one who does not perform attendance. And it is not to be spoken to one who finds fault with Me, the Supreme Lord, who censures Me by superimposing faults from the human standpoint.
word_for_word: evaṃ gītārtha-tattvam upadiśya tat-saṃpradāya-pravartane niyamam āha — idam iti
having thus taught the truth of the meaning of the Gītā, he states a rule for setting its tradition in motion with ‘this’
idaṃ gītārtha-tattvaṃ te tvayā atapaskāya sva-dharma-anuṣṭhāna-hīnāya na vācyam
this truth of the meaning of the Gītā is not to be spoken by you to one without austerity, one lacking performance of his own dharma
na ca abhaktāya gurau īśvare ca bhakti-śūnyāya kadācid api na vācyam
nor is it ever to be spoken to one without devotion, one devoid of devotion to the teacher and to the Lord
na ca aśuśrūṣave paricaryām akurvate vācyam
nor is it to be spoken to one unwilling to serve, one who does not perform attendance
māṃ parameśvaraṃ yaḥ abhyasūyati
one who finds fault with Me, the Supreme Lord
manuṣya-dṛṣṭyā doṣa-āropeṇa nindati
who censures Me by superimposing faults from the human standpoint
tasmai ca na vācyam
to him also it is not to be spoken

68.translation: He states the fruit for the teacher of the Gītā scripture who teaches it to My devotees who are free of these faults, with ‘who.’ The one who will explain it among My devotees, who will state it to My devotees, performs supreme devotion to Me. Then, becoming free of doubt, he attains Me alone. This is the meaning.
word_for_word: etaiḥ doṣaiḥ virahitebhyaḥ mad-bhaktebhyaḥ gītā-śāstra-upadeṣṭuḥ phalam āha — ya iti
he states the fruit for the teacher of the Gītā scripture who teaches it to My devotees who are free of these faults, with ‘who’
mad-bhakteṣu abhidhāsyati mad-bhaktebhyaḥ yaḥ vakṣyati
the one who will explain it among My devotees, who will state it to My devotees
sa mayi parāṃ bhaktiṃ karoti
performs supreme devotion to Me
tataḥ niḥsaṃśayaḥ san mām eva prāpnoti iti arthaḥ
then, becoming free of doubt, he attains Me alone: this is the meaning

69.translation: And further, with ‘and not.’ Among human beings there is no other person more highly pleasing to Me than the expositor of the Gītā scripture to My devotees. Nor will there be one at another time. And for Me also there is now on earth no one dearer than him, nor will there be at a later time. This is the meaning.
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — na ca iti
and further, with ‘and not’
tasmāt mad-bhaktebhyaḥ gītā-śāstra-vyākhyātuḥ sakāśāt anyaḥ manuṣyeṣu madhye
among human beings, another than the expositor of the Gītā scripture to My devotees
kaścid api mama priya-kṛttamaḥ atyantaṃ paritoṣa-kartā na asti
there is no person more highly pleasing to Me, one who causes extreme satisfaction
na ca kāla-antare bhavitā bhaviṣyati
nor will there be one at another time
mama api tasmāt anyaḥ priyataraḥ adhunā bhuvi tāvat na asti
and for Me also there is now on earth no one dearer than him
na ca kāla-antare api bhaviṣyati iti arthaḥ
nor will there be at a later time: this is the meaning

70.translation: He states the fruit for one who recites with ‘will study.’ The one who will study, will recite as japa, this righteous dialogue between us, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, which does not depart from dharma—by that person I would be worshipped with the sacrifice of knowledge, the best of all sacrifices. This is My thought. Although that person, not understanding the meaning of the Gītā, merely recites it, nevertheless, when I hear it, the thought arises in Me that he is making Me alone manifest. Just as in the world, if someone even accidentally, sometime, utters someone’s name, that person, thinking ‘this one is calling me,’ comes near him, so I too would become present near him. Therefore I have been pleased by Ajāmila, Kṣatrabandhu, and others through mere utterance of the Name somehow; in just the same way I would be pleased with this person also. This is the meaning.
word_for_word: paṭhataḥ phalam āha — adhyeṣyate iti
he states the fruit for one who recites with ‘will study’
āvayoḥ kṛṣṇa-arjunayoḥ imaṃ dharmyaṃ dharmāt anapetaṃ saṃvādam
this righteous dialogue between us, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, which does not depart from dharma
yaḥ adhyeṣyate japa-rūpeṇa paṭhiṣyati
the one who will study, will recite as japa
tena puṃsā sarva-yajñebhyaḥ śreṣṭhena jñāna-yajñena aham iṣṭaḥ syām bhaveyam iti me matiḥ
by that person I would be worshipped with the sacrifice of knowledge, the best of all sacrifices; this is My thought
yady api asau gītārtham abudhyamāna eva kevalaṃ japati
although that person, not understanding the meaning of the Gītā, merely recites it
tathā api mama tat śṛṇvataḥ mām eva asau prakāśayati iti buddhiḥ bhavati
nevertheless, when I hear it, the thought arises in Me that he is making Me alone manifest
yathā loke yadṛcchayā api kaścit kadācit kasyacit nāma gṛhṇāti
just as in the world, if someone even accidentally, sometime, utters someone’s name
tadā asau mām eva ayam āhvayati iti matvā tat-pārśvam āgacchati
that person, thinking ‘this one is calling me,’ comes near him
tathā aham api tasya sannihito bhaveyam
so I too would become present near him
ata eva ajāmila-kṣatrabandhu-pramukhānāṃ kathaṃcit nāma-uccāraṇa-mātreṇa prasannaḥ asmi
therefore I have been pleased by Ajāmila, Kṣatrabandhu, and others through mere utterance of the Name somehow
tathā eva asya api prasanno bhaveyam iti arthaḥ
in just the same way I would be pleased with this person also: this is the meaning

71.translation: He states the fruit also for another person who hears while another recites, with ‘faithful.’ The person who is endowed with faith, even if he merely hears. To turn away the fault-finding thought, ‘why does some faithful person recite aloud?’ or ‘he recites incoherently,’ he says ‘and without envy.’ One who hears without envy, free of fault-finding, he too, freed from all sins, may attain the worlds of those who have performed merits such as the Aśvamedha.
word_for_word: anyasya japataḥ yaḥ anyaḥ kaścit śṛṇoti tasya api phalam āha — śraddhāvān iti
he states the fruit also for another person who hears while another recites, with ‘faithful’
yaḥ naraḥ śraddhā-yuktaḥ kevalaṃ śṛṇuyāt api
the person who is endowed with faith, even if he merely hears
śraddhāvān api kaścit kim-artham uccaiḥ japati abaddhaṃ japati iti vā doṣa-dṛṣṭiṃ karoti
the fault-finding thought, ‘why does some faithful person recite aloud?’ or ‘he recites incoherently’
tad-vyāvṛtti-artham āha
to turn that away, he says
anasūyaḥ ca asūyā-rahitaḥ yaḥ śṛṇuyāt
one who hears without envy, free of fault-finding
sa api sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ muktaḥ san
he too, freed from all sins
aśvamedha-ādi-puṇya-kṛtān lokān prāpnuyāt
may attain the worlds of those who have performed merits such as the Aśvamedha

72.translation: With the intention ‘if correct understanding has not arisen, I will instruct again,’ he says ‘has it?’ ‘Kaccit’ has the sense of a question. Delusion from ignorance is inversion produced by ignorance of reality. The rest is clear.
word_for_word: samyag-bodha-anutpattau punaḥ upadekṣyāmi iti āśayena āha — kaccit iti
with the intention ‘if correct understanding has not arisen, I will instruct again,’ he says ‘has it?’
kaccit iti praśna-arthe
‘kaccit’ has the sense of a question
ajñāna-saṃmohaḥ tattva-ajñāna-kṛto viparyayaḥ
delusion from ignorance is inversion produced by ignorance of reality
spaṣṭam anyat
the rest is clear

73.translation: Having attained his purpose, Arjuna said, with ‘destroyed.’ Delusion concerning the Self is destroyed. Because memory in the form of recollection of one’s own nature—‘this is what I am’—has been obtained by me through Your grace. Therefore I stand; I am present for battle. I am one whose doubt concerning dharma has gone. I will carry out Your command.
word_for_word: kṛtārthaḥ san arjuna uvāca — naṣṭa iti
having attained his purpose, Arjuna said, with ‘destroyed’
ātma-viṣayo moho naṣṭaḥ
delusion concerning the Self is destroyed
yataḥ ayam aham asmi iti svarūpa-anusandhāna-rūpā smṛtiḥ tvat-prasādāt mayā labdhā
because memory in the form of recollection of one’s own nature—‘this is what I am’—has been obtained by me through Your grace
ataḥ sthitaḥ asmi yuddhāya upasthitaḥ asmi
therefore I stand; I am present for battle
gataḥ dharma-viṣayaḥ saṃdeho yasya saḥ aham
I am one whose doubt concerning dharma has gone
tava ājñāṃ kariṣye iti
I will carry out Your command

74.translation: Having thus narrated the dialogue of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sañjaya, reconnecting with the story at hand, said ‘thus.’ I heard, have heard, the hair-raising, horripilating dialogue. The rest is clear.
word_for_word: tad evaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ prati śrī-kṛṣṇa-arjuna-saṃvādaṃ kathayitvā
having thus narrated the dialogue of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna to Dhṛtarāṣṭra
prastutāṃ kathām anusandadhānaḥ saṃjaya uvāca — iti iti
Sañjaya, reconnecting with the story at hand, said ‘thus’
roma-harṣaṇaṃ romāñca-karaṃ saṃvādam aśrauṣam śrutavān aham
I heard, have heard, the hair-raising, horripilating dialogue
spaṣṭam anyat
the rest is clear

75.translation: He states the possibility of his own hearing it with ‘by Vyāsa’s grace.’ Divine sight, hearing, and so forth were given to me by the Blessed Vyāsa. Therefore, by Vyāsa’s grace I have heard this. What was it? In answer he says: the supreme yoga. He makes its supremacy manifest: I heard it directly from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Yoga, Himself speaking it.
word_for_word: ātmanaḥ tat-śravaṇe saṃbhāvanām āha — vyāsa-prasādāt iti
he states the possibility of his own hearing it with ‘by Vyāsa’s grace’
bhagavatā vyāsena divyaṃ cakṣuḥ-śrotra-ādi mahyaṃ dattam
divine sight, hearing, and so forth were given to me by the Blessed Vyāsa
ataḥ vyāsasya prasādāt etat ahaṃ śrutavān asmi
therefore, by Vyāsa’s grace I have heard this
kiṃ tat iti apekṣāyām āha paraṃ yogam
what was it? in answer he says: the supreme yoga
paratvam āviṣkaroti
he makes its supremacy manifest
yogeśvarāt śrī-kṛṣṇāt svayam eva sākṣāt kathayataḥ śrutavān iti
I heard it directly from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Yoga, Himself speaking it

76.translation: And further, with ‘O King.’ ‘I rejoice’ means ‘I become horripilated’ or ‘I obtain joy.’ The rest is clear.
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — rājan iti
and further, with ‘O King’
hṛṣyāmi romāñcito bhavāmi harṣaṃ prāpnomi iti vā
‘I rejoice’ means ‘I become horripilated’ or ‘I obtain joy’
spaṣṭam anyat
the rest is clear

77.translation: And further, with ‘and that.’ ‘That’ points to the universal form. The rest is clear.
word_for_word: kiṃ ca — tat ca iti
and further, with ‘and that’
tat iti viśva-rūpaṃ nirdiśati
‘that’ points to the universal form
spaṣṭam anyat
the rest is clear
